title: Remote Exercise for Atraumatic Cuff Health - REACH Trial
official: Remote Exercise for Atraumatic Cuff Health - REACH Trial
summary: This study aims to assess outcomes from physical therapy treatment traditionally delivered in-person and physical therapy delivered via telehealth in patients with atraumatic rotator cuff tears. This will be a single center, parallel arm randomized trial within the Orthopaedic Surgery Department at Baylor Scott \& White (BS\&W). Eligible participants indicated for physical therapy for atraumatic rotator cuff tears will be enrolled, consented, and randomized, in a 1:1 scheme, into two study arms. Arm 1 will consist of a standardized in-person physical therapy program. Arm 2 will consistent of a standardized physical therapy program to be delivered exclusively over telehealth video conference. Outcomes of interest are the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI) at 6-months and 12-months following completion of assigned physical therapy arm. Secondary outcomes are ASES, SF-12, MHI, FABQ, PSQ-8, and TUQ.

interventions.name: Standardized Physical Therapy Program Delivered through Telehealth

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 40 years and older
* Shoulder pain and/or loss of range of motion, strength or function
* MRI-confirmed partial- or full-thickness supraspinatus and/or infraspinatus tear of 4 centimeters or less in the longitudinal dimension
* Ability and willingness to provide informed consent
* Absence of glenohumeral osteoarthritis on x-rays
* No isolated subscapularis and/or teres minor tear

Exclusion Criteria:

* Primary diagnosis of something other than a rotator cuff tear
* History (in last 2 years) of shoulder fracture involving the humeral head on affected side
* Contraindication to MRI (claustrophobia, pacemaker, pregnancy, shoulder implant, etc.)
* Receiving Worker's Compensation
* Acute rotator cuff tear caused by severe trauma
* Grade 4 fatty infiltration (any tendon)
* Surgical candidates on presentation or prior rotator cuff surgery
